root_cause.text: Missing skb deallocation in error handling paths after mt76_connac_mcu_alloc_sta_req() allocates an skb, when intermediate functions (mt76_connac_mcu_sta_wed_update, mt76_connac_mcu_sta_key_tlv) fail before the skb is sent via mt76_mcu_skb_send_msg(), causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "mt76_connac_mcu_alloc_sta_req() allocates an skb which is expected to be freed eventually by mt76_mcu_skb_send_msg(). However, currently if an intermediate function fails before sending, the allocated skb is leaked." The patch adds `dev_kfree_skb(skb)` in the error paths of `mt76_connac_mcu_sta_ba`, `mt76_connac_mcu_add_key`, `mt7915_mcu_add_sta`, and `mt7925_mcu_add_key` before returning on failure.

This statement lacks error handling; if mt7915_mcu_sta_he_tlv fails (e.g., due to memory allocation), the previously allocated skb is never freed, causing a memory leak.
Similar to the previous, this call has no return check or deallocation, so a failure here would also leak the skb.
This is the final point where the skb is sent. If an intermediate function (e.g., mt76_connac_mcu_sta_wed_update) fails before this line, the skb is not freed, matching the root cause.
This TLV allocation is part of the skb construction. If subsequent calls fail, the skb (including this TLV) is leaked due to missing deallocation.

This check handles allocation failure, but the missing deallocation for later failures is the core issue. This statement itself is not vulnerable, but it is part of the sequence that lacks proper cleanup.
